entries.meaning: When paying a memory cost, you may banish this card from your graveyard to pay 1 of that cost. Check any Class Bonus or level condition attached to it.
Apply the marked effect only when your champion shares a class with the card. It is not an extra cost.
The marked effect requires the named champion. For example, a Lorraine Bonus is active for Lorraine, not every Warrior.
The marked effect requires your champion to share an element with this card.

A bracketed threshold applies only when its condition is met: Level checks champion level, Memory counts cards in memory, and Damage counts damage on your champion. A plus sign means at least that amount.
LV means your champion’s current level, including applicable modifiers. X is a variable defined by that card’s effect or chosen cost; read the accompanying sentence.

Your lineage is the whole champion stack, including its top card, earlier levels, and other cards added there. A named Lineage restriction requires the matching champion. Inner lineage excludes the top champion card.
This ability applies to your champion while its card is in that champion’s lineage. Read Curse effects too: inheritance can be harmful.
Activate the ability by banishing its card from your champion’s inner lineage. Check its additional restrictions; the top champion card is not in the inner lineage.
These abilities trigger when the object enters or leaves the field. Read the event literally: moving a card between hand and memory does not make it enter the field.
This triggers when the unit attacks, before damage. It does not require a successful hit.

entries.term: On Hit / On Champion Hit / On Ally Hit
entries.meaning: A hit requires combat damage. On Champion Hit and On Ally Hit require damage to that kind of unit. Fully prevented damage does not cause a hit.
A unit dies when it goes from the field to the graveyard. On Death triggers for that unit. On Kill requires a kill from combat damage, not a later damage effect. Banishing a unit is not a death.
These trigger when the specified event happens. If sacrificing a Potion pays its ability’s cost, its On Sacrifice trigger resolves before that Potion ability.
While awake, this unit must be chosen before other objects you control for opponents’ attacks when possible. Resting it switches off that protection.
When your champion is attacked, an awake ally with Intercept may redirect the attack to itself. Keep that ally awake if you need this protection.
Stealth prevents a unit from being targeted by attacks. True Sight allows attacks to target units with Stealth. Neither is general immunity to card effects.
Spells cannot target this object. An effect that does not target can still affect it.
This attack ignores Taunt and cannot be intercepted. Other restrictions and defensive effects can still matter.
Attack all legal attackable objects controlled by one chosen player, including siegeable domains. That attack cannot be intercepted or redirected. Each defending unit can retaliate.
Look at the specified number of cards from the top of your deck. Return any to the top in any order and the rest to the bottom in any order. This is not a draw.
Reduce this card’s activation cost by your champion’s level. A higher effective level can make it cheaper; it does not automatically increase the card’s damage.

ruleQuote.text: This card costs LV less to activate

entries.meaning: The next Spell you activate this turn activates and resolves with the stated extra effective levels. This does not replace your champion card or unlock an advanced element.
Remove the stated number of damage counters from your champion. Recovery removes damage; it does not raise the life stat.
Weapons use durability counters. Wielding a weapon removes one during combat’s damage step. At zero durability, a regalia weapon goes to banishment; a non-regalia weapon goes to the graveyard.
Each buff counter gives its object +1 power and +1 life. Keep counters visible so attack and survival calculations stay clear.
You may spend three enlighten counters on your champion to draw a card. Some cards spend them differently or prevent spending them.
Distant lasts until the end of that unit’s controller’s turn. Ranged N gives its attacks +N power while it is distant. Distant alone does not stop attacks or damage.

An intent holds the attack cards used by an attacker during combat. Loading puts cards underneath another card; weapon loads enter the attacker’s intent when wielded as the rules allow. Follow the card’s loading restrictions.
These weapon types must be loaded before attacking and cannot be combined with an attack card. Bullets and Aethercharges follow their own loading instructions.
If this card would be banished from the field or an intent, return it to its owner’s material deck instead. You still need a way to materialize or load it again.

While looking at this card during a glimpse, you may activate it for its Starcalling cost. Put the other cards from that glimpse on the bottom in any order. Element and other activation requirements still apply.
While looking at this card during a glimpse, you may load it into an Aetherwing you control. Check Element Bonus when the ability has that condition.
This object enters rested. It cannot pay a rest cost until awake.

ruleQuote.text: This object enters the field rested.

entries.meaning: The unit wakes up at the beginning of your end phase. This can leave an attacker ready to protect you on the opponent’s turn.
At your recollection phase, a Foster ally becomes fostered if it has taken no damage since your previous turn ended. It becomes fostered only once; resolve its On Foster ability then.
Banish the specified ally, then return it under its owner’s control at the beginning of the next end phase. It returns as a new object.
The card goes to its owner’s material deck preserved at the time specified. During materialization, you may take a preserved card back to hand instead of materializing.

The ally obeys only while your champion meets the stated level. Below that level you cannot attack with it or activate its abilities, but it may still retaliate. Its static and triggered abilities still apply; follow any additional requirements.
Harmonize labels a bonus for having activated a Melody that turn. Check the card’s own wording and play a Melody before the Harmony that needs it.
Gather summons a random Herb from the six named Herb tokens. Herbs have subtypes such as Adjuvant or Catalyst; use those exact subtypes when checking a Potion’s recipe.

You may sacrifice the listed ingredients instead of paying the card’s reserve cost. Brew can appear on Potions or other cards, including allies. Brewing a Potion puts it into play; activating its sacrifice ability is a separate step.
This label checks the relationship between hand and memory. Scale of Souls requires equal card counts at its recollection trigger to recover.
Stop the specified card activation from resolving. Follow the negating effect for where its card goes; some effects let its controller pay to avoid negation.
You may activate this card at fast speed when you have an opportunity to act, including during the opponent’s turn. You must still meet its other requirements.
Add the named card from outside the game to the specified zone. Keep the required physical generated cards with your deck.
Put the specified token onto the field. Use its own card text and stats. Tokens are separate objects, even when represented with counters or a token board.
An omen is a card in banishment with an omen counter on it. Only those marked cards count for Ciel’s omen requirements; ordinary banished cards do not.
A mastery is a player ability provided by a card. Keep its reference visible. Shifting Currents starts North and has four directions; use its diagram for adjacent moves.

This object cannot be sent from the field to the graveyard, including by destruction or sacrifice. It can still be banished or returned by appropriate effects. Damage is not prevented; if temporary Immortality ends, existing damage can become lethal.
A Link attaches to the specified kind of object and is sacrificed if its link breaks. Link Shield can destroy the attachment instead of the linked object and clears that object’s temporary damage.
When an arcane unit deals combat damage, eligible static counters can be spent for extra damage to the object it damaged. Use the counter’s rules and its location; this is extra non-combat damage.
Your Aenean Spells activate and resolve with +2 effective champion levels while you control an object with this ability. Multiple Elysian Auras do not add further +2 bonuses.
Reveal cards from the top of your deck until you find the specified kind of card or reach the stated limit. Put the found card in hand and the rest on the bottom in random order.
These counters have the effect stated on the card. Crimson Vein uses them to raise your champion’s life and gains another when you recover.
While paying a reserve cost, you may rest this object to pay 1 of it. Resting it may stop you using another ability that also needs it awake.
Banishment and graveyard are different zones. Banishing moves a card to banishment; discarding normally puts it in the graveyard. Effects that name one zone cannot use cards in the other.
Destroy the object you control as instructed. A sacrificed ally dies if it goes to the graveyard; sacrificing a Potion also enables any On Sacrifice trigger it has.
Damage prevention cannot reduce this damage. It still counts as damage and can defeat a champion.
An upright object is awake; turn it sideways to rest it. It must be awake to pay a rest cost. Waking it up makes it upright again. Allies normally enter awake unless an effect says otherwise.

Materializing plays a card from your material deck. During your materialize phase, you normally get one materialization. An effect can grant another, but you still pay its costs unless it says otherwise. Regalia are equipment and other material-deck cards.
Spell is a card subtype, not a name for every action. Empower affects Spells; Spellshroud protects against targeting by Spell sources. Check the card’s type line.
A Curse is a subtype. These decks can put Curse cards into a champion’s lineage, where their inherited effects apply. Read whose lineage receives the card; some effects can curse your own champion.
Exalted is enabled while you have another advanced element enabled. Pure Cytosynth still needs that elemental access; an effective-level boost alone does not provide it.

A Domain is a field object, not an ally. Siegeable Domains can be attacked and lose durability when damaged. Other Domains, such as Obelisks, follow their own text; do not assume every Domain is siegeable.

Phantasia is a card type; Fractal is a subtype. Count the exact category named by an effect. An effect that counts Fractals does not count every phantasia, and an opponent’s phantasias do not count as ones you control.

Diao Chan uses glimmer counters to pay the reserve cost of a Reaction Spell activated from memory through her inherited rest ability. Remove one counter per reserve paid; this ability is usable only on an opponent’s turn.
Reaction is a card subtype. Check the type line: an effect that permits a Reaction Spell from memory does not permit every action or every fast card.

At the beginning of a player’s main phase, each object they control with wither counters must be sacrificed unless they pay 1 per counter on it. The wither counters are then removed. These are not damage counters.

A Flowerbud has no effect on its own. Bloom cards replace opposing Flowerbuds with your chosen tokens: Lycoria damages its controller, Baihua heals its controller’s opponents, Floodbloom banishes cards from its controller’s deck, and Nightshade adds wither to its controller’s objects.

Play a double-faced card on its default side. Transform flips the same object to its other face; its counters and rested state remain unless the effect says otherwise. It does not enter again. Use the new face’s rules; outside the field, use the default face.

Guo Jia stores quest counters on his champion. Fabled Azurite Fatestone can rest and remove ten to wake and transform into Seiryuu. Counters are spent only when the relevant effect tells you to remove them.

Prepare N lets you remove N preparation counters from your champion as an optional additional activation cost. The card becomes prepared only if you pay it. Other abilities can spend the same counters, so budget offense and defense together.

Agility N returns up to N cards of your choice from memory to hand at the beginning of the end phase. It can work on an opponent’s turn too. This is not a draw and does not empty memory unless N is large enough.

entries.pattern: ambush|retaliate against attackers while not defending
entries.meaning: An awake unit with Ambush may retaliate against an attacker even when it is not the defender, including when another player’s object is attacked. It still needs to be able to retaliate.
Retort N gives an ally +N power while it is retaliating. It does not boost that ally’s own attacks.

ruleQuote.text: As long as this ally is retaliating, it gets +N power.

entries.meaning: These phantasia ally tokens have Unblockable and prevent 3 damage per instance. They may attack only units your champion has dealt combat damage to during the current turn. A non-combat damage spell does not open a target for them.
Influence is the total number of cards in your hand and memory. Moving cards between those zones does not change the total.

Revealing shows a card without moving it unless the effect says otherwise. Luxem cards may trigger when revealed from memory, with their Class and Element Bonuses enabled. Placing cards revealed into memory for Imbue is not revealing them from memory.

You may reserve cards face up while activating an Imbue card. If enough meet the listed requirement, the card becomes imbued. Ordinary Imbue checks matching element; other versions specify their own requirement. Turn those payment cards face down after activation.
Critical N doubles combat damage unless an opponent discards N cards. In multiplayer, any opponent may pay, even one who is not being attacked.

This status taxes attacks against your objects by 1 per declaration. When an activation, materialization, or trigger targets your object, you may negate it unless its controller pays 1. You lose the status when an opponent gains it.

A siegeable domain can be attacked and takes damage by losing durability counters. At zero it is destroyed. On Destroy triggers when its object is destroyed, including by a destruction effect; merely returning it to hand is not destruction.

Age counters do only what the card says. Some accumulate during recollection, while Polaris gains them from sacrificed Herbs. Read each payoff: counters may determine damage, extra draws, or generated cards.

These counters have card-specific effects. Essence Crucible adds Spell damage, Photic Blade gains power, and Verdant Scepter spends counters to buff Slimes and draw. A counter does not grant these effects to every card.

Follow the host card’s text. Pendant of Accrual spends debt for draws; Worn Diary uses page counters; Sabela marks a returned regalia with a bond; Flourishing Qi counts charge on its pending activation. These counters do not inherently increase power or life.
Each debuff counter gives its object −1 power and −1 life. Reducing an ally to zero life can destroy it; this is not dealing damage.
D6 means roll a fair six-sided die when resolving the effect. Use that result in the stated calculation; do not assume the highest roll.

A copy follows the effect that creates it. Copying an activation is different from activating another card yourself. A copied object normally uses the printed face, without existing counters or temporary bonuses. Check any special instructions on the copy effect.

Each level counter gives the champion +1 effective level. This can meet Pride and ordinary Level thresholds, but does not change its base level, skip champion levels, or unlock an advanced element by itself.

Sheen counters mark a unit or your Fractured Memories. Cards with a Sheen threshold, like Sheen 8+, check the counters on your Fractured Memories. A Memorite Obelith token moves its sheen counters to Fractured Memories when it leaves the field.
You may activate the card from your graveyard by paying its Ephemerate cost. The card becomes ephemeral in the intent.
Luxem is an advanced element. Some effects delevel your champion, which lowers its level and can stop level-based bonuses until you level up again.
You can have only one card with Divine Relic in your material deck. Flawless Spirit of Mordred can only level up into a Mordred champion.
Distortion is an object type. Some cards care whether an object is a Distortion, or turn token copies of regalia into Distortions.
